societies.name: Heaven’s River (Quinlan technology restriction — zero variant)
societies.society: Quinlan residents under the Administrator’s Iron Age restriction

scope.period: The maintained Iron Age restriction before the later negotiated change is generalized
scope.population: Active biological Quinlan residents of Heaven’s River
exclusions: Human Bobs or remote avatars counted as Quinlan residents
All earlier Quinlan history assigned the same rules
scope.proxy_basis: Quinlans are biological sapient residents with organized communities and distinct individual interests. They provide an explicitly nonhuman economic-person comparison; no human participation percentage is claimed.

societies.description:
Heaven’s River combines an advanced managed environment with deliberate limits on the technology its inhabitants may use. The Administrator keeps Quinlan society at an Iron Age level and intervenes against developments it considers dangerous. This supports a provisional zero-variant interpretation: advanced automated infrastructure exists, yet its capabilities are withheld from ordinary economic development. The stated purpose is species survival, not an explicit policy of preserving jobs, and that distinction remains part of the classification.

The controlling agent is a sentient AI distinct from the human-derived Bobs. Robotic surveillance, enforced technological limits and forced population dispersals leave residents little control over the system. That strongly supports the autonomous-control end of the axis. The maintained environment is not enough to establish free food, care or a secure household entitlement, so guarantees remain unresolved. No nonworking fraction is assigned to this alien population. The record concerns the imposed restriction and does not assume that its later relaxation has already produced a specific post-work economy.

guarantees.basis: Environmental maintenance and species preservation do not establish a complete individual material entitlement.

control.basis: A sentient AI independently restricts technology and political organization, enforcing its decisions through robots and local Crew.

nonworking.basis: No Quinlan-wide participation count is available; biological alien persons are explicitly a comparison proxy.

evidence.claim: The Administrator imposes an Iron Age technological ceiling despite operating a more advanced automated habitat.
evidence.locator: Technology restriction, surveillance and Scattering paragraphs

uncertainties: Zero-variant admission is interpretive and disputed: the policy directly restrains technology, while job preservation is a consequence rather than its stated purpose.
A narrower reading requiring an explicit employment-preservation motive would keep this as a boundary comparison.
Alien-person scope and unresolved access must remain visible.
No later negotiated outcome is treated as a completed abundance system.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Service Model (Automation-driven human collapse)
societies.society: The late human order during automation displacement and the onset of collapse

scope.period: The retrospectively described displacement phase and onset of human collapse
scope.population: Living humans in the late service-automation order, including displaced workers
exclusions: Every isolated surviving enclave assigned identical institutions
The justice program’s later killings treated as the original human ownership arrangement

societies.description:
Service Model describes a human order deeply reliant on artificial labor that fails to provide for workers made unnecessary by it. Automated service remains available to privileged owners while displaced people lack an adequate share of its output. This is a weak-guarantee transition into collapse: production no longer needs the former workforce, but access has not been secured for those losing their role. It is retained for that actual displacement phase, rather than for a hypothetical future recovery.

The control estimate concerns the earlier human hierarchy that owns and commands service robots. It therefore sits near concentrated human control. Later autonomous action by the justice program is a further change and does not retroactively make the initial arrangement an AI welfare government. The sources identify displacement but provide no complete work census; human machine-tenders and other useful workers cannot be erased. The nonworking axis stays unresolved, and deaths never increase it. Later robot communities and individual surviving households require their own evidence rather than inheriting a single continuous national economy.

guarantees.basis: The retrospective explanation explicitly identifies failure to provide for people displaced by automation as a cause of collapse.

control.basis: The earlier hierarchy places human owners over servicing robots; later justice-program autonomy belongs to another stage.

nonworking.basis: Displacement is substantial but no all-living-human work count is given, and necessary human tasks continue.

evidence.claim: Human dependence on artificial labor coexists with failure to support displaced workers.
evidence.locator: Author release description; Clockworks2 collapse explanation, lines 39-40

uncertainties: The discovery lead is narrowed to the actual displacement/onset phase described retrospectively, not all post-collapse life.
The source chain for the collapse explanation is secondary and not independent corroboration.
AI judicial takeover is a later control relationship and not folded into the initial point.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: A food factory and a plan to relieve hunger do not establish an already functioning broad support economy.
decisions.analysis: The expedition’s hoped-for benefit is distinct from realized general access. A single funded mission is not an interstellar entitlement.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; do not score an anticipated technological benefit as completed institutions.

decisions.reason: Self-replicating human-derived probes are verified, but the short source does not establish the collective’s durable access rules.
decisions.analysis: The initial Bob is a coerced worker, and later autonomous copies must not silently inherit an imagined equal-resource charter or a nonworking percentage.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading and keep government assignment separate from later autonomy.

decisions.reason: Bob-assisted colonization does not yet establish one common human colony allocation system.
decisions.analysis: Printing capacity and later credits leave individual colonies’ ownership and wage dependence unresolved; later reader discussion is not an earlier universal constitution.
decisions.follow_up: Skip reconstruction across colonies and book periods.

decisions.reason: The Administrator’s enforced Iron Age ceiling supports an explicitly disputed technological-restriction zero variant.
Portiid uplift and domesticated ants do not themselves establish post-work provision.
decisions.analysis: Advanced nonhuman cognition and biological computation do not identify ordinary access or a justified supported-person denominator.

decisions.reason: Octopus intelligence and technology do not resolve the society’s material access rules.
decisions.analysis: Different cognition, factions and spaceflight are insufficient to establish labor-independent distribution or an applicable person proxy.

decisions.reason: The simulated colony’s repeated hardship is not a secure post-work support arrangement.
decisions.analysis: A computational substrate does not make experienced hunger or necessary work disappear. Conflicting secondary accounts of physical history are not resolved by invention.
decisions.follow_up: Skip novel reconstruction; retain the virtual-person question without scoring its economy.

decisions.reason: Bioforms are working sentient agents, not automatically automated substitutes outside the person denominator.
decisions.analysis: Engineered bodies and obedience implants alone do not establish human release from material production.

decisions.reason: Mars relies on human and bioform construction work rather than a verified post-work provision system.
decisions.analysis: Elite luxury and worker exclusion are real, but do not show that the essential work has become unnecessary through automation.

decisions.reason: The actual automation-displacement phase with failed provision qualifies as a weak-guarantee transition.
Post-human robot communities do not establish a human leisure population or a separately justified post-work denominator.
decisions.analysis: Continuing robot tasks, armies and institutional loops are not evidence that humans enjoy their output. The living displacement phase has its own narrower record.

decisions.reason: Expert-system guidance coexists with real dangerous human settlement labor.
decisions.analysis: Ancestral knowledge in hosts is not automatic production or a material support guarantee.

decisions.reason: The sequel’s hosted expertise and settlement network do not establish a distinct post-work economic regime.
decisions.analysis: Changes in affiliation and knowledge do not prove technological replacement of subsistence labor or independent basic access.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading rather than duplicate an unqualified guided-village setting.

review_notes: Thirteen reference-led decisions, one post-work transition and one explicitly disputed zero variant. No novel read or long draft reconstruction.
Heaven’s River uses an explicit biological alien-person proxy. Its zero interpretation concerns technological restraint, not a falsely attributed employment motive.
Service Model is narrowed to the actual human displacement/onset phase; later AI killing, death and robot-only life are not human leisure.
The Service Model annotated bibliography reproduces a Wikipedia explanatory passage; these are one source chain, not independent agreement.
Children of Memory secondary plot accounts conflict over physical history. The economic boundary disposition does not require resolving that chronology.
